Cuts any input down to exactly 10 ticks (half a second), however long it is held: the input makes a note block play, a sound sensor (calibrated sculk sensor) hears it and switches on for exactly 10 ticks, and a comparator reading a chest tunes the sensor to note blocks only, so footsteps, dropped items and a lever switching off never set it off. The smallest vibration-proof 10 gt pulse limiter (5 blocks); shorter inputs come out as 10 ticks too. Detail: the note block plays only when it becomes powered (note_block_play, frequency 10); the chest's 1111 cobblestone make the comparator output 10 into the sensor's back, and a calibrated sensor with a back signal accepts that frequency only (the lever's block_deactivate is 9, footsteps 1, items landing 2, blocks broken or placed 12 and 13).

Cuts any input down to exactly 30 ticks (1.5 seconds), from just 2 blocks, for quiet builds: the input makes a note block play, and a sound sensor (sculk sensor) that hears it switches on for exactly 30 ticks. It hears every other sound too, so it only works where nobody walks or drops items within 8 blocks and where the input arrives by a long line, not from a lever next to it. The smallest 30 gt pulse limiter; shorter inputs come out as 30 ticks too. Detail: the note block plays only when it becomes powered (note_block_play); the sensor is 1.4 blocks away (diagonal, so its own power never replays the note) and stays active 30 gt (SculkSensorBlock.ACTIVE_TICKS).

A single observer facing the input sends a 2-tick pulse every time the input turns on or off (an observer fires whenever the block it faces changes): the smallest dual-edge detector, 1 block. Read from the observer itself, copies stand side by side every block. Inputs of 4 ticks or more: a shorter one ends while it is still firing.

An observer watches a lamp that the input lights: the lamp turns on at once and goes off 4 ticks after the input, so the observer pulses 2 ticks on both edges even for a 1-tick input (an observer facing the input itself needs 4). Read from the observer, copies stand side by side every block.

An observer facing the input sends a pulse on every change of the input, and the repeater behind it (on a block) stretches each pulse to 4 ticks, its delay: a dual-edge detector of 4 ticks in 3 blocks. Read from the repeater, copies stand side by side every block. Inputs of 8 ticks or more.

An observer facing the input sends a pulse on every change of the input, and the repeater behind it (on a block) stretches each pulse to 6 ticks, its delay: a dual-edge detector of 6 ticks in 3 blocks. Read from the repeater, copies stand side by side every block. Inputs of 15 ticks or more.

The input lights a lamp, which goes off 4 ticks after the input does; an observer watching the lamp pulses on each change, and a repeater stretches each pulse to 4 ticks: a dual-edge detector of 4 ticks for inputs of 4 ticks or more, half what the observer facing the input needs. Read from the repeater, copies stand side by side every block.

An observer and two sticky pistons: when the input turns on, the pistons move the observer so its pulse is not seen; when the input turns off, the observer fires in front of the output: a 2-tick pulse on every falling edge, the smallest falling-edge detector (3 blocks). Copies stand side by side every block. Inputs of 4 ticks or more.

A sticky piston pushes an observer into the output cell whenever the input turns on, where it fires one 2-tick pulse; it is pulled back when the input turns off and fires out of sight: the smallest 2-tick pulse limiter (2 blocks). Copies stand side by side every block. Inputs of 4 ticks or more.

A sticky piston pushes an observer into the output cell when the input turns on, where it fires one 2-tick pulse; pulled back when the input turns off, it fires out of sight: the smallest rising-edge detector (2 blocks). Copies stand side by side every block. Inputs of 4 ticks or more.

A copper bulb flips each time the input turns on (never when it turns off, even for a 1-tick input), a comparator reads the bulb, and an observer watching the comparator turns each flip into a 2-tick pulse: a rising-edge detector that sees 1-tick inputs. Read from the observer, copies stand side by side every block.
